facts.statement: The genus was known from fossils found in the Late Cretaceous Los Llanos Formation in Argentina.
facts.quote: known from the Late Cretaceous Los Llanos Formation in Argentina

facts.statement: The genus contains only a single species, L. tamaensis.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, L. tamaensis.

facts.statement: The genus was described by Fiorelli et al. in 2016.
Llanosuchus lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Llanosuchus belongs to the parent group Notosuchia.
Llanosuchus is classified as a reptile.
Only one fossil occurrence of Llanosuchus has been recorded.

rejected.statement: Llanosuchus is an extinct genus of notosuchian mesoeucrocodylian.
